name: Controlled fusion route portfolio
description: A paid-domain candidate map comparing major controlled-fusion product routes by their route-specific dependencies and shared power-plant constraints. Primary routes are separated from secondary routes so immature concepts are not presented as equivalent to better-evidenced paths.

targetContext.targetScale: grid-relevant pilot plant or commercial power-plant pathway
targetContext.targetPerformance: net electric output, maintainable plant availability, closed fuel cycle, durable materials, credible cost path
targetContext.targetUseCase: firm low-carbon electricity and high-load industrial power
targetContext.region: US investor-facing research across global public, private, and government-heavy routes

name: Controlled fusion power capability
description: The demand-side capability: economically useful controlled fusion power, not just plasma gain or isolated ignition.

name: Primary route family
description: Routes with the clearest public evidence base for first-pass comparison: tokamak, stellarator, and laser inertial fusion energy.

name: Tokamak magnetic-confinement route
description: Primary magnetic-confinement route using a toroidal plasma, large external magnets, plasma current, heating/current-drive systems, divertor heat exhaust, tritium/blanket interfaces, remote maintenance, and power conversion. This controlled-fusion route node intentionally replaces the older commercial-fusion fixture node for the paid-domain map.

name: Secondary route family
description: Routes that should be visible but not treated as equal first-screen peers until route-specific evidence and exposure improve: magnetized target, FRC, and Z-pinch.

name: Shared plant constraint stack
description: Cross-route plant constraints: tritium/fuel cycle, blanket and heat extraction, plasma-facing or chamber materials, remote maintenance, regulation, net electric gain, and plant availability.

name: Stellarator magnetic-confinement route
description: Magnetic-confinement route using optimized three-dimensional external coils for steady-state plasma confinement with less reliance on large plasma current than tokamaks.

name: Laser inertial fusion energy route
description: Inertial-fusion-energy route using high-power laser drivers to compress fuel targets at high repetition rate; its bottlenecks are laser wall-plug efficiency, target factories, target injection, chamber survivability, and fuel recycling.

name: Magnetized target / liquid-metal compression route
description: Secondary magneto-inertial route using magnetized plasma plus mechanical or liquid-metal compression. Liquid metal is modeled as part of this route's compression, first-wall, blanket, and heat-extraction architecture rather than as a standalone fusion route.

name: Field-reversed configuration route
description: Secondary compact magnetic route based on a self-contained field-reversed plasma configuration, with route-specific dependencies around formation, sustainment, high-beta stability, heating, diagnostics, and possible direct energy conversion.

name: Z-pinch pulsed-power route
description: Secondary route where very high pulsed current creates the magnetic compression field. The route is dominated by pulsed-power hardware, MHD stability, electrodes or liners, chamber lifetime, and repetition economics.

name: Tokamak current drive and heating
description: Neutral beam, RF, and current-drive systems used to reach and sustain fusion-relevant plasma conditions.

name: Tokamak divertor heat exhaust
description: Divertor and heat-exhaust system for particle and energy removal under high plasma flux.

name: Tokamak disruption mitigation
description: Prediction, avoidance, and mitigation of plasma disruptions that can damage reactor components.

name: Tokamak cryogenic magnet plant
description: Cryogenic plant, quench protection, power supplies, and superconducting magnet operating infrastructure.

name: Tokamak remote-maintenance interface
description: In-vessel component replacement and hot-cell logistics needed for availability in an activated tokamak plant.

name: Stellarator 3D coil system
description: Non-planar superconducting coils that create the optimized stellarator magnetic field; manufacturing and assembly precision are central bottlenecks.

name: Stellarator coil metrology and manufacturing
description: Precision fabrication, metrology, transport, and assembly of complex 3D coils.

name: Stellarator field optimization
description: Magnetic-field optimization for confinement, turbulence reduction, alpha-particle behavior, and reactor geometry.

name: Stellarator steady-state heating
description: External heating and control path for long-pulse or steady-state stellarator operation.

name: Stellarator blanket and maintenance access
description: Blanket, shield, first-wall, and remote-maintenance access inside a 3D magnetic geometry.

name: Laser driver efficiency and repetition rate
description: High-efficiency, high-repetition laser driver needed for power plants; NIF-style ignition is not itself plant net-electric gain.

name: Target fabrication and injection
description: Repeatable, low-cost fuel target manufacturing, cryogenic handling, injection, and tracking at power-plant repetition rates.

name: Laser IFE chamber wall and optics
description: Chamber, final optics, debris handling, wall lifetime, and target debris mitigation for repeated laser shots.

name: Laser IFE pulse balance of plant
description: Thermal recovery, repetition-rate plant systems, tritium processing, and recirculating power for pulsed laser fusion plants.

name: Laser IFE target fuel cycle
description: Tritium loading, recovery, inventory control, and target throughput for inertial fusion energy.

name: Diode-pumped laser array supply
description: Laser diode and driver hardware supply for efficient repeated laser shots.

name: Cryogenic target factory
description: Factory process for precision cryogenic fusion targets at useful cost and repetition rate.

name: MTF plasma injector
description: Forms and injects magnetized plasma before compression.

name: Liquid-metal liner compression
description: Liquid-metal cavity or liner that compresses plasma and can also act as first wall, neutron blanket, and heat transfer medium.

name: MTF compression driver
description: Mechanical, pneumatic, electromagnetic, or pulsed driver system for repeatable symmetric compression.

name: Liquid-metal compatibility and tritium extraction
description: Liquid-metal chemistry, corrosion, activation, tritium breeding/extraction, and inventory control.

name: MTF mechanical system lifetime
description: Fatigue, sealing, cavitation, shock, and service life for pulsed compression hardware.

name: MTF pulse heat extraction
description: Liquid-loop heat extraction, isolation, pumping, and power conversion for repeated pulses.

name: FRC formation and sustainment
description: Formation, merging, translation, sustainment, and stabilization of a compact field-reversed plasma.

name: FRC neutral beam and current drive
description: Heating and current-drive path for compact FRC plasmas.

name: FRC high-beta stability
description: Physics and control of high-beta compact plasma stability and confinement scaling.

name: FRC diagnostics and control
description: Fast diagnostics and controls for short-lived compact plasma operation.

name: FRC direct energy conversion
description: Potential direct conversion interface for charged-particle energy where applicable; highly route-specific and unproven at plant level.

name: FRC repetition lifetime
description: Hardware lifetime and repeatability under many compact-plasma pulses or operating cycles.

name: Z-pinch pulsed-power driver
description: Capacitors, switches, transmission, pulse shaping, and high-current delivery for Z-pinch compression.

name: Z-pinch sheared-flow or pinch stability
description: MHD instability control method required to keep pinched plasma together long enough for useful fusion conditions.

name: Z-pinch electrode or liner lifetime
description: Erosion, replacement, liquid-metal cooling, or liner lifetime under high-current repeated pulses.

name: Z-pinch fuel injection and preparation
description: Fuel delivery, plasma preparation, gas distribution, or target/liner preparation for repeated Z-pinch shots.

name: Z-pinch high-repetition chamber
description: Chamber, cooling, debris handling, and service design for many repeated high-current pulses.

name: Z-pinch energy recovery and power conversion
description: Pulse energy recovery, power conditioning, and plant-scale power conversion for pulsed operation.

name: Breeding blanket and heat extraction
description: Neutron blanket, tritium breeding, heat extraction, coolant compatibility, and structural integration across most D-T power-plant routes.

name: Tritium breeding and fuel cycle
description: Fuel-cycle branch requiring lithium-bearing breeding material, neutron multipliers where used, tritium extraction, inventory control, containment, accountancy, and regulatory safeguards. Modeled as a shared D-T plant constraint rather than as a route-specific supplier exposure.

name: Plasma-facing components and divertor
description: First wall, divertor, armor, cooling channels, erosion control, neutron-damage tolerance, and remote replacement strategy. This controlled-fusion node keeps first-wall/divertor constraints inside the paid-domain route map instead of pulling the older commercial-fusion fixture node.

name: Remote maintenance system
description: Remote inspection, in-vessel component replacement, hot-cell logistics, activated-material handling, maintenance scheduling, and plant-availability engineering for fusion power plants.

name: Superconducting magnet system
description: Toroidal/poloidal field coils, central-solenoid-like systems where applicable, superconducting cable or HTS tape, cryostat, quench protection, power supplies, and cryogenic plant. Modeled as a magnetic-route infrastructure constraint, not an all-route dependency.

name: Fusion neutron materials lifetime
description: Damage, activation, helium production, erosion, corrosion, and inspection lifetime for materials exposed to fusion neutrons and plasma or chamber loads.

name: Fusion regulatory and safety case
description: Licensing, tritium inventory, activated materials, worker safety, environmental case, and grid interconnection for fusion plants.

name: Fusion exposure status: private/government-heavy
description: Most route builders in this map are private companies, government labs, or international projects. Public-market exposure should be treated as supplier exposure, not direct pure-play fusion equity.

name: Net electric gain
description: Plant-level metric comparing usable electric output to recirculating and input power over realistic operating cycles. This controlled-fusion metric is separate from older commercial-fusion fixture metrics so the paid route map does not inherit legacy topology.

name: Fusion plant availability factor
description: Economic maturity metric for how often a fusion plant can generate electricity after maintenance, in-vessel component replacement, tritium-plant outages, and materials-lifetime constraints.

name: HTS tape supply chain
description: High-temperature-superconductor tape and conductor chain for compact high-field magnets; supplier exposure is route-specific and unreviewed.

name: Magnet quench protection and power supply
description: Protection and power electronics needed to operate large superconducting magnets safely.

name: ITER Organization
description: International tokamak project; government/international exposure, not a listed equity.

name: Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics
description: Government/research organization behind Wendelstein 7-X stellarator work; not a listed equity.

name: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory / NIF
description: US national-lab laser inertial confinement facility; not a listed equity.

name: Sandia Z Machine
description: US national-lab pulsed-power and Z-machine program; not a listed equity.

name: General Fusion
description: Private magnetized target fusion company; not directly purchasable as public stock.

name: TAE Technologies
description: Private FRC/aneutronic-fusion route builder; not directly purchasable as public stock.

name: Helion Energy
description: Private FRC-style fusion company; not directly purchasable as public stock.

name: Zap Energy
description: Private sheared-flow-stabilized Z-pinch company; not directly purchasable as public stock.

name: Xcimer Energy
description: Private laser inertial fusion energy company; not directly purchasable as public stock.

name: Bruker
description: Public supplier candidate for superconducting and scientific-instrument exposure; not a pure-play fusion route builder.

name: Furukawa Electric
description: Public Japan-listed conductor/material supplier candidate; not a pure-play fusion route builder.

name: Oxford Instruments
description: Public London-listed cryogenic and scientific-instrument supplier candidate; not a pure-play fusion route builder.
